passages.original: ludi quam amplissimi ut fierent senatus decreuit. ad eos ludos auctore Attio Tullio uis magna Uolscorum uenit. priusquam committerentur ludi, Tullius, ut domi compositum cum Marcio fuerat, ad consules uenit; dicit esse quae secreto agere de re publica uelit. arbitris remotis, 'inuitus' inquit, 'quod sequius sit, de meis ciuibus loquor.
passages.english: The senate decreed that the games should be held on the grandest possible scale. To these games, at the instigation of Attius Tullius, a great number of Volscians came. Before the games began, Tullius, as had been arranged at home with Marcius, came to the consuls and said that there were matters concerning the state that he wished to discuss in private. When witnesses had been sent away, he said: 'It is against my will that I speak of my own fellow citizens in a way that reflects worse on them.
passages.notes: 'quod sequius sit' is taken as 'something rather unfavourable'; the phrase could also be read as 'what may be taken amiss'.
